stories.headline: 3.2-Magnitude Earthquake Jolts Pulwama, Tremors Felt Across Kashmir
stories.title: 3.2-Magnitude Earthquake Jolts Pulwama, Tremors Felt Across Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 05: A mild earthquake measuring 3.2 on the Richter scale struck Pulwama district in Jammu and Kashmir on Monday evening, sending tremors through parts of south and central Kashmir. According to seismic data, the earthquake was recorded at 6:44 pm at a shallow depth of around 5 kilometres. The epicentre was located approximately 28 kilometres southeast of Srinagar, at coordinates 33.890°N latitude and 74.992°E longitude. Given its shallow depth, the tremor was felt in several adjoining areas, particularly across parts of south and central Kashmir. No reports of casualties or damage to property had emerged immediately following the earthquake.

stories.title: SC refuses to entertain PIL on recurring Assam floods, asks authorities to take remedial measures
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, while declining to entertain the plea filed by advocate Ujjawal Gaur, directed the registry to forward a copy of the petition to all the respondent authorities, asking them to look into the issues raised and take appropriate remedial measures.

article_sentences: A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, while declining to entertain the plea filed by advocate Ujjawal Gaur, directed the registry to forward a copy of the petition to all the respondent authorities, asking them to look into the issues raised and take appropriate remedial measures.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking directions to ensure effective measures to prevent recurring floods, riverbank erosion and drainage-related problems in Assam and the Brahmaputra Valley.
Appearing in person, Gaur submitted that the administrative lapses highlighted in the petition were amenable to judicial scrutiny and urged the apex court to issue notice to the authorities.

However, the CJI Kant-led Bench observed that the various suggestions and deficiencies highlighted by the petitioner ought to draw the attention of the concerned authorities, but the issue was "not essentially legal" in nature.
Declining to entertain the PIL, the top court directed its registry to forward the petition to all the respondents, who would look into its contents and take appropriate remedial measures.

The plea had sought judicial intervention to ensure effective implementation of the statutory framework governing flood and erosion management and had proposed, among other measures, a high-level expert mechanism to examine the recurring problems.

The petitioner had contended that the recurring devastation caused by floods could not be treated as wholly inevitable when statutory frameworks and specialised institutions had been created for flood control, bank erosion and drainage management.

The plea referred to the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980, the Assam Embankment and Drainage Act, 1953 and the River Boards Act, 1956, arguing that these laws contemplated scientific investigation, integrated river-basin planning and implementation of measures relating to floods, erosion and drainage.

It relied on successive reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) which, according to the petitioner, had recorded deficiencies in flood-control planning, execution and maintenance, drainage management, floodplain management and monitoring of projects.

The petition specifically referred to the CAG's Performance Audit on "Flood Control in Assam", contained in Report No. 5 of 2018, which, it claimed, identified deficiencies in integrated basin-wise planning, floodplain zoning, hydrological and morphological studies, execution and monitoring of flood-control works.

It also relied on official records concerning drainage congestion, backflow, inadequate drainage through sluices, encroachment upon natural drainage channels, sedimentation and river morphology as factors aggravating flood vulnerability.

The petitioner further highlighted a shortage of technical manpower in the Brahmaputra Board, referring to an official Lok Sabha reply dated December 12, 2024, which disclosed that 65 of its 182 sanctioned technical posts remained vacant in 2024.

stories.headline: Nepal wraps up Rasuwa flood search; shifts focus to rehabilitation, reconstruction
stories.title: Nepal wraps up Rasuwa flood search; shifts focus to rehabilitation, reconstruction
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Oct 5: Nepal on Monday concluded the search and rescue operation launched after the devastating August 26 flash floods, which claimed at least 1,455 lives, and is now shifting its focus to rehabilitation and reconstruction, officials said. The decision was taken at the 21st meeting of the National Council of the NDRRMA chaired by Prime Minister Balendra Shah at the Singha Durbar Secretariat here, the Prime Minister's Office said. The government decided to wind up the 40-day search and rescue operation, except for essential activities. The meeting directed concerned agencies to expedite rehabilitation and reconstruction works in the areas affected by the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods. "The decision was taken based on recommendations from the District Security Committee, District Disaster Management Committees, the Executive Committee of the NDRRMA, as well as findings from field inspections," it said. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has confirmed 1,455 deaths, 5,285 people missing and 13,795 rescued in the disaster.

stories.headline: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.title: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.summary: While a businessline analysis reveals a striking geographical overlap between high voter removals and TVK victories, experts urge caution against reading it as a conspiracy
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) have stirred protests not just at the national but at the State level too.
In Tamil Nadu, DMK president and former Chief Minister MK Stalin has recently said that the deletion of several lakh voters was one of the reasons for his party’s loss.
The social media is abuzz about how TVK victory may have been aided by these deletions.
A businessline analysis of the granular data on SIR deletions and the outcome of the TN assembly elections in 2026, throws us some interesting trends.
TVK has struggled to win in constituencies where the SIR deletions were lower but has recorded more wins in constituencies where the deletions were higher.
Political analysts and experts however warn that not much should be read into these numbers.
We compared the net reduction in voter count in each constituency as per the April 2026 electoral roll with pre-SIR numbers.
Of the total 234 constituencies, 19 constituencies had lower deletions, of up to 10,000 voters.
In these, the TVK won 2 seats, the DMK 7, the AIADMK 6 and others 4.
Eighty constituencies had deletions between 10,000 to 20,000 voters.
The TVK won 22 of these constituencies, the DMK 20, the AIADMK 24 and others 14.
Sixty-six constituencies had deletions between 20,000 to 30,000.

stories.headline: SC Notices to ECI, Centre; Demand for CEC Resignation Grows
stories.title: SC Notices to ECI, Centre; Demand for CEC Resignation Grows
stories.summary: The controversies relating to several decisions taken by the Election Commission of India, including the amendments made to Form 6, will now be examined by the Supreme Court.
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The controversies relating to several decisions taken by the Election Commission of India, including the amendments made to Form 6, will now be examined by the Supreme Court.
If any decision is found to be not in accordance with the law, it will be annulled.
The apex court on Monday issued notices to the EC and the Centre on pleas alleging that the poll body took several decisions without the approval of the two other Election Commissioners.
However, the Supreme Court refused to pass any interim order restraining CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking any decision until the final disposal of the petitions.

The bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, said that it may examine the immunity clause in the law that provides protection to the CEC even after he demits office.
“You know the power of the court,” the bench said, pointing out that the immunity granted to the CEC is something that even judges do not have.
Meanwhile, former Election Commissioner S. Y. Quraishi, in a post on X, said that a deleted voter cannot use Form 6, as it is intended for first-time voters.

He said, “All those who have been forced to fill it have committed a criminal offence carrying a one-year prison sentence,” while Election Commission officials “who forced them are abettors to the crime.”
Officials, however, disputed the claim.
Quraishi was of the view that CEC Gyanesh Kumar should resign on moral grounds.
He said the position of CEC had become untenable and had caused chaos and harassment to crores of people.
A Journey of Three Decades Time passes faster than we realise.

stories.headline: Samvidhaan Pe Charcha 4.0 at Parul University Connects Constitutional Thought with Contemporary Legal Practice
stories.title: Samvidhaan Pe Charcha 4.0 at Parul University Connects Constitutional Thought with Contemporary Legal Practice
stories.summary: Parul University held the fourth edition of its flagship legal conclave, Samvidhaan Pe Charcha 4.0. The event was attended by eminent members of the judiciary, senior advocates, legal professionals and law students for a series of discussions on constitutional values, contemporary legal questions and the changing landscape of law. The conclave had expert addresses, interactive sessions, PU Talks, workshops and competitive platforms, giving students an opportunity to interact with the legal fraternity beyond the classroom. The proceedings featured Hon’ble Mr. Justice Vipul M. Pancholi , Judge, Supreme Court of India, Hon’ble Mr. Justice D.N. Ray , Judge, High Court of Gujarat, Hon’ble Mr. Justice N.S. Sanjay Gowda , Judge, High Court of Gujarat, Shri Gaurav Bhatia , Senior Advocate, Supreme Court of India and National Spokesperson, BJP, Ms. Mahalakshmi Pavani , Senior Advocate, Supreme Court of India, and Ms. Anitha Shenoy , Senior Advocate, Supreme Court of India, alongside other distinguished members of the legal fraternity. Their presence provided an opportunity for aspirant lawyers to hear first hand the views of the judiciary and to learn about the practical aspects of legal education and advocacy. Reflecting on the relevance of constitutional principles to the legal profession and spotlighting the future lawyers, Hon’ble Mr. Justice Vipul Manubhai Pancholi said , “A law school has a responsibility not merely to impart legal knowledge but also to nurture professional ethics, constitutional values and social responsibility. Therefore, the lawyer of the future must not only know the law but also understand the society and technology within which the law operates. As future advocates, remember that advocacy is not merely about winning but about assisting the court in reaching a just and legally sound conclusion.” Addressing the audience, Hon’ble Mr. Justice D.N. Ray shared his perspective on constitutional and legal issues along with his thoughts on how today's youth is facing the challenges that come with the fast growing world. He said “ In this age of instant gratification and instant success, please be prepared to fail, which is the most important lesson which nobody will ever tell you. It is okay to fail. There's no problem. So the most important thing is to fail and to live on with all these experiences and to understand that there is no competition which you are actually fighting. Your only competitor is You yourself.” The proceedings also included an interactive engagement followed by aPU Talk by Shri Gaurav Bhatia, Senior Advocate, Supreme Court of India and National Spokesperson, BJP on “The Living Constitution: Democracy, Rule of Law & Changing Landscape of Fundamental Rights” . This session discussed the relevance of the constitutional principles and the changing understanding of the basic rights in contemporary India. Bringing the discourse closer to the present constitutional scenario and emphasizing the need to understand constitutional principles within the framework of an evolving society, he said “ The Constitution is a document which talks about equality, liberty, fraternity, justice. What is the purpose of life if you can't be treated with dignity? More important than even existence. Life is not about breathing. Life is about adding soul to your lifespan, and dignity is that soul.” Talking to the students on the topic of the Indian Constitution then, now, and tomorrow , Hon’ble Mr. Justice N.S. Sanjay Gowda , Judge, High Court of Gujarat, said “ A constitution is a document which basically creates us. The basic requirement of the constitution is not to tell us what we can do, but what we cannot and we should not do.” On the occasion, Dr.Devanshu Patel, President, Parul University said, “Samvidhaan Pe Charcha is an endeavor to bring constitutional thought into meaningful dialogue with the next generation of legal professionals. By meeting judges, advocates and experts, students gain perspectives that complement their academic learning and that motivate them to take a more active interest in the principles, responsibilities and realities of the legal profession.” The conclave also acknowledged the performance of law students of Parul University in various prestigious national competitions. Sachidanand Patil, Jay Gawalni and Ishant Suthar, winners of 11th Shri N. J. Yasaswy Memorial Moot Court Competition 2026 hosted by ICFAI Law School, Hyderabad were congratulated along with Priyodarshini Roy, Best Speaker at National Moot Court Competition 2026 organised by Innovation Institute of Law, New Delhi. Kunj Prajapati also received a Special Mention at the largest debate conference of JG University, Gujarat and Swayam Prakash Shukla won a Bronze Verbal Mention in AIPPM . Moot Court Competition was the continuation of the competitive proceedings of Samvidhaan Pe Charcha 4.0, with Quarter Final and Semi-Final rounds being held in English and Gujarati, offering a practical platform for students to put their legal research, argumentation and advocacy skills into practice in front of experienced legal professionals. The academic program also featured workshops on “Innovation Vs. Regulation: Finding the Constitutional Balance in the Digital Economy” by Mr. Nihit Nagpal and “Samvidhan or Adhikar: Equality, Liberty & Dignity in Contemporary India” by Mr. Zafar Khurshid . The competitions in English and Gujarati provided students with a chance to put their legal reasoning and advocacy skills to the test in a competitive environment. The three-day conclave concluded with addresses by senior members of the judiciary, an interactive session of Q&A with students and the felicitation and prize distribution of participants. Hon’ble Mr. Justice Surendra Pandey, Judge, Patna High Court , spoke on constitutional values, human dignity and judicial responsibility and asked students to think about litigation and contribute to the justice-delivery system. He reminded them, adding “ You don't have to become enemies only because the other person has a different point of view,” and added “The judges do not own the constitution. they have just been given the duty to interpret it. It's owned by all of us.” Justice Soman Sen, Chief Justice, Kerala High Court , shared his views on Fundamental Rights, Article 21, constitutional morality, the Emergency, basic structure and challenges presented by new technologies . He said, “We may leave this auditorium today, but the constitution cannot remain inside it.” He also stressed the importance of thought and reasoning in legal advocacy: “The strength of an argument does not come from the volume in which it is delivered, but from the quality of thought behind it.” Speaking about the career paths of young lawyers, Justice N. Koteshwar Singh, Judge, Supreme Court of India , advised the students to look into the emerging areas like AI, cybercrime, forensic science and patents and also advised them not to make money their first priority. “Don't think of money when you start,” he said and stressed “The most important is the dignity of the individuals. That is the core.” His advice to the students was simple: “Be a smart lawyer.” Students asked questions on regional diversity in the judiciary, social media algorithms, delays in criminal trials, religious and civil disputes, prolonged incarceration, NDPS cases and the right to speedy trial during the last interaction. The event culminated with the prize distribution of 3rd State Moot Court Competition (Gujarati) and 4th Inter-University Moot Court Competition 2026 with the prize money of Rs 15,000 to Rs 60,000 in the former and Rs 40,000 to Rs 1.75 lakh in the latter. Samvidhaan Pe Charcha 4.0 united judicial wisdom, professional perspectives and student advocacy, providing law students with a platform to engage with the Constitution, contemporary legal questions and the realities of the justice system through dialog, competition and direct interaction with leading legal minds. (The views, opinions, and claims in this article are solely those of the author’s and do not represent the editorial stance of The Assam Tribune)

stories.title: Shaktikanta Das Says India Within Striking Distance Of 8% Growth
stories.summary: Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, highlights India’s strong economic resilience despite a challenging global environment marked by wars, fragmentation, technological blockades, energy price volatility and rising inflation. He points out that India’s real GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter of the current financial year, supported by strong domestic demand and investment. Das also notes that India recorded an average annual GDP growth of 7.9% during the five-year post-COVID period from FY22 to FY26. Taking the period from July-September 2025-26 to April-June 2026-27 into account, he says India’s real GDP growth slightly exceeds 8%. Das reiterates his earlier view that India is “within a striking distance of 8% growth,” even as global growth faces significant challenges.

The petitioner seeks to ensure that State Human Rights Commissions remain fully functional in compliance with Section 21 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and the Supreme Court's directions in DK Basu.
State of West Bengal.

Qua Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Meghalaya, the petitioner seeks replacement of prolonged Acting Chairperson arrangements with substantive appointments.
The petition also prays for the States to provide SHRCs with the required administrative, investigative and technical staff, including senior government and police personnel.
It further seeks publication of annual reports on SHRC websites and in the public domain, alongwith their placement before the respective state legislatures.

stories.headline: 'Women In Delhi Must Feel Safe Even Walking Alone At Night; Men Should Fear Committing Sexual Offences' : Supreme Court To Police
stories.title: 'Women In Delhi Must Feel Safe Even Walking Alone At Night; Men Should Fear Committing Sexual Offences' : Supreme Court To Police
stories.summary: "As police, you must live up to the expectations of the people, and people shouldn't run away from you," the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "As police, you must live up to the expectations of the people, and people shouldn't run away from you," the Court said.

Hearing the suo motu case taken on the rising sexual offences in the National Capital Region, the Supreme Court today(October 5) in the strongest terms expressed the need to take all preventive steps to prevent offences against women.

While addressing the general feeling that women are not safe in Delhi, it ordered that all public places such as the metro, bus stands, railways stands must be continuously monitored by beat patrolling units, and halting points of Delhi police control room vans must be strengthened.
Additionally, it stressed that, given the festive season is approaching, the miscreants will be on the run, so the police need to ensure that the women are safe.
"You need to create a fright or fear in the mind of a man who is prone to commit offences.
Unless and until you don't create that fright or fear in that goon or anti-social element that 'ab kuch kia toh mar jayenge', you will not be able to prevent commission of such crimes...
Every girl molested is our sister, our mother.
Huge challenge for NCT Delhi police.
Don't allow such things to happen," the Court orally said.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran recently took suo motu cognisance of repeated incidents of rape, including a gangrape of a minor in a park and the alleged sexual assault of a minor inside a moving sleeper bus in Delhi.

Expressing distress over the news reports, the Court appointed Senior Advocate Liz Mathew as amicus and issued a slew of directions divided into two parts: immediate directions, such as intensified patrolling, and other long-term directions.
Today, the matter came up subsequent to the directions issued, in which the amicus was supposed to submit further suggestions.

stories.headline: 'Don't Let Doubts Of Others Limit Your Achievements': Gujarat High Court Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal To Women Lawyers In Farewell Speech
stories.title: 'Don't Let Doubts Of Others Limit Your Achievements': Gujarat High Court Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal To Women Lawyers In Farewell Speech
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: While speaking at her farewell reference on Monday (October 5), Gujarat High Court Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal asked women lawyers in the profession not to let circumstances, expectations and doubts of others to determine the limits of their achievements.
The Chief Justice asked the women lawyers in the profession who are already established to hold the hands of those female bar members who are climbing up as well as guide them in the profession.
Notably, the Central government today notified Justice Agarwal's elevation to the Supreme Court.
"And to the young women in the profession, you are the foremost in my mind in a lot of what I do.
My goal is to make this institution a beautiful place for you where you can find yourself and achieve whatever you seek and deserve.
Do not allow circumstances, expectations and doubts of others to determine the limits of your achievements.
In my career I have met the same obstacles as you.
And it was perseverance which carried me through.

To the women already established in the profession, on the bench or at the bar, whichever rung of the professional ladder you stand on today, hold the hands of those who are climbing up, guide them, nurture them and give them the confidence to persevere".
At the outset, Justice Agarwal said that she finds it difficult to leave the High Court which over the years had assumed immense significance in her life.
"Last 3 years have been a turning point for my professional and personal growth…these years taught me to keep going despite the difficulties around me.
To stay grounded and to keep working without losing my grit," the judge said.

stories.headline: RBI expected to raise Repo Rate to 5.50%; what it means for loan EMIs
stories.title: RBI expected to raise Repo Rate to 5.50%; what it means for loan EMIs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in title weight 42
article_sentences: With inflation firming and global central banks tightening, the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee is widely expected to end its extended pause and raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%.
The move, if announced, would be India’s first rate hike since February 2023—and could gradually push up EMIs on home, auto and business loans.
The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is meeting at a delicate moment, with domestic inflation ticking upward even as major global central banks tighten policy aggressively.

Market participants and economists increasingly expect the RBI to begin a shallow tightening cycle with a measured 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate, taking it from 5.25 per cent to 5.50 per cent.
The six-member MPC began its October review on Monday and is scheduled to announce its decision on October 7.
A 25-bps move, if announced, would be the first repo-rate increase since February 2023, after the central bank held the rate unchanged through four consecutive policy reviews in 2026.
The policy dilemma has sharpened against a backdrop of aggressive rate increases by the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan to combat persistent inflation.
However, Ajitabh Bharti, Executive Director and Co-founder of CapitalXB, argues that India’s macroeconomic position gives the RBI more room for calibration than many of its global peers.
“India cannot pursue a one-to-one alignment with global rate trajectories.
The RBI must balance currency stability and internal liquidity management without over-tightening into a still-moderate inflation environment,” Bharti said.
He pointed out that headline inflation averaged just 1.9 per cent between April 2025 and February 2026, well below the RBI’s 4 per cent medium-term target.

While inflation has risen more recently -- retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August, remaining above target for a third consecutive month -- the broader price environment remains comparatively contained.

body: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is meeting at a delicate moment, with domestic inflation ticking upward even as major global central banks tighten policy aggressively.

Market participants and economists increasingly expect the RBI to begin a shallow tightening cycle with a measured 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate, taking it from 5.25 per cent to 5.50 per cent.
The six-member MPC began its October review on Monday and is scheduled to announce its decision on October 7.
A 25-bps move, if announced, would be the first repo-rate increase since February 2023, after the central bank held the rate unchanged through four consecutive policy reviews in 2026.
The policy dilemma has sharpened against a backdrop of aggressive rate increases by the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan to combat persistent inflation.
However, Ajitabh Bharti, Executive Director and Co-founder of CapitalXB, argues that India’s macroeconomic position gives the RBI more room for calibration than many of its global peers.
“India cannot pursue a one-to-one alignment with global rate trajectories.
The RBI must balance currency stability and internal liquidity management without over-tightening into a still-moderate inflation environment,” Bharti said.
